top_p: provider default, unreported (the kumori router sends none and reports none)
schedule: Start by simplifying the goal and hypotheses using simp.
claim: none: an exploratory pilot (n=45, about 9% power for the paper's 19 wins vs 3 losses split; ~170 targets for 80%). It checks the lane answers 16 times per target through the router and estimates discordance. A confirmatory run, if any, is sized from it and frozen in its own manifest; pilot rows are never pooled into it.
endpoint: kernel acceptance within 16 calls (pass@16, early stop at first accept), per target per arm; secondary: calls, HTTP requests, tokens, seconds
primary: skeleton vs alone, exact two-sided sign test on the targets only one arm solved (the 2026-10-28 rule)
scope: operational re-solving of public solved targets; not unseen-theorem generalization; model memorization of public miniF2F/NNG is not ruled out
adaptation: the paper prefixes a completion model's output with the skeleton; a chat lane is asked in the prompt to begin with it, and each row counts the answers that did (skeleton_followed)
source: Burton, Structured Hints for Sample-Efficient Lean Theorem Proving, arXiv 2601.16172, Appendix A (read 2026-11-08)
